Current Status and Daily Life  
• No significant changes; taking things one day at a time.  
• Stays home when not at work; spends time with family.  
• No major personal issues reported, but some frustration due to inability to provide for daughter yet (no paycheck since returning home).  
• Daughter will be seven in April; happy to have him home.  

Job Search and Employment Preferences  
• Plans to apply for morning shift jobs (bakery or dishwashing).  
  ◦ Prefers these jobs to be after Turn90 commitments.  
• Interested in warehouse/forklift positions for long-term employment.  
  ◦ Has some experience with Skill Cat and forklift operation.  
  ◦ Warehouses are located near current residence.  
• Target distribution center considered a good opportunity ($22/hour starting pay), but location restrictions apply.  
• Will look into both short-term (bakery/restaurant) and long-term (warehouse) job options.  
• Has a resume from previous employment ("from inside").  

Legal and Supervision Constraints  
• Possesses Social Security card, birth certificate, and photo ID/permit.  
• Currently on community supervision/probation for a crime committed in Lugoff/Elgin area.  
  ◦ Paid restitution for damages to victim’s truck.  
  ◦ No permanent restraining order, but cannot be in area of victim during supervision period (two years).  
  ◦ Not allowed to work in Lugoff/Elgin area while on supervision.  
  ◦ No issues with victim; victim did not want prison time, only restitution.  
• Not on child support; no other legal requirements reported.  
• Should have driver’s license soon.  

Transportation Needs  
• Working on obtaining a vehicle for work transportation.  
  ◦ Has access to rides currently, but limited by location restrictions.  
  ◦ Family members may help with acquiring a car.  
  ◦ Considering a car lot in Columbia offering $100 down and $150–$200/month payments.  
  ◦ Saving paychecks for vehicle purchase; food stamps would help manage expenses.  
• Occasionally, donated cars become available through the organization; will be considered for future donations.  

Food Assistance and Benefits  
• Still needs to connect with PPAC food stamp office; previous attempts unsuccessful.  
  ◦ Attempted to complete required class, but system did not work.  
  ◦ Plans to try again on Friday when off work.  
  ◦ May seek help from Kat or Daisy during Thursday lab time if issues persist; Jen can facilitate contact.  

Community Engagement and Turn90 Involvement  
• Will attend a job fair to speak about Turn90 experience and its impact during and after incarceration.  
  ◦ Invited by Amy; will share personal story and program benefits.  
• Expresses gratitude for support and is at peace with current progress.  

Family Support and Responsibilities  
• Mother (age 70) works at Burns Chicken for 35 years; currently working extra due to staff shortages.  
  ◦ Mother and partner help with transportation and phone work.  
• Wants to maintain ability to attend Turn90 and pursue additional evening work (5:00–9:00 or 5:00–11:00 PM).  

Action Items and Next Steps  
• Will apply for bakery/dishwashing jobs and explore warehouse/forklift opportunities.  
• Will retry food stamp application on Friday; may seek additional help if needed.  
• Organization will look for short-term and long-term job leads and keep him in mind for vehicle donations.  
• Will continue saving money for vehicle purchase.  
• Will participate in job fair to represent Turn90.  
• Will reach out if further assistance is needed.

Recently released from MacDougal. Needs help with job placement and also wants to be on T90 waitlist. Has an appointment at VocRahab already. Will look for temp jobs in the meantime. 

Housing Situation  
• Staying with his partner, who is applying for a condominium off Forest Drive.  
 ◦ They are temporarily in a motel for two weeks due to the previous neighborhood being undesirable.  
 ◦ Partner is gathering pay stubs for the condo application; approval process is ongoing.  
 ◦ The leasing office lost contact but reconnected after Justin’s release; more documents needed for approval.  
• Can stay with his mother if needed but currently has a roof over his head.

Employment Search and Vocational Rehabilitation  
• Actively seeking work and considering vocational rehabilitation (voc rehab) for support.  
 ◦ Plans to get barber tools via voc rehab; needs a friend’s barbershop to sign a job offer document.  
 ◦ Will present job offer, release papers, and other documents to voc rehab for a voucher for barber equipment.  
• Open to any job to generate income, including dishwashing, food service, and bakery work.  
 ◦ He has baking skills and a resume prepared for such positions.  

Personal Documentation and Transportation  
• Obtained his social security card and birth certificate.  
• Plans to visit the DMV to retake the permit test, as his permit expired and cannot be simply renewed.
Had trouble with Google Meet, rescheduled him to tomorrow.
